title: Promise: Property Mining for Sequential Synthesis
problem: Sequential synthesis for removing redundant circuit logic depends critically on accurate invariant generation, but existing techniques are problem-specific or rely on localized reasoning, limiting their applicability to diverse circuit designs with modular composition.
motivation: Modular hardware design creates opportunities for redundancy removal through state unreachability, but existing invariant generation is too limited to be generally useful across different circuits.
method: Proposes Promise, a fast circuit redundancy removal strategy that exploits rich information from simulation traces to infer global circuit invariants using efficient polynomial-time algorithms. Identifies relations between signals and registers that hold in all reachable states. Integrates with high-level synthesis tools to optimize generated circuits and aid other sequential synthesis procedures.
key_novelty: First trace-based global invariant inference approach for sequential synthesis using polynomial-time algorithms, enabling practical redundancy removal in HLS-generated circuits.
contributions: Trace-based global invariant mining from simulation data
Polynomial-time algorithms for efficient invariant inference
limitations: Evaluation focused on HLS-generated circuits; applicability to manual designs unclear; scalability to very large circuits not discussed.
primary_theme: Trace-based invariant mining for circuit synthesis
